To file a cashless health insurance claim, the policyholder must get treatment at a network hospital and submit a pre-authorization form to the Third Party Administrator (TPA) before or within 24 hours of admission for emergency cases.
For reimbursement claims, the policyholder pays the hospital bill upfront and submits original bills, discharge summary, and diagnostic reports to the insurer within 15 to 30 days of discharge.
Health insurance policies typically have an initial waiting period of 30 days during which no claims are payable except for accidental injuries.
Pre-existing diseases under a health insurance policy are usually covered only after a waiting period of 2 to 4 years from the policy start date.
A free-look period of 15 to 30 days allows a new health insurance policyholder to cancel the policy and receive a refund if they are not satisfied with the terms.
If a health insurance premium is not paid by the due date, insurers typically offer a grace period of 15 to 30 days during which the policy remains in force.
Health insurance claims can be rejected if the treatment was for a condition excluded under the policy, such as cosmetic surgery or self-inflicted injury.
Room rent sub-limits in a health insurance policy cap the reimbursable amount for hospital room charges as a percentage of the sum insured.
A co-payment clause requires the policyholder to bear a fixed percentage of the claim amount, commonly used in senior citizen health insurance policies.

Health insurance portability allows a policyholder to switch insurers while retaining continuity benefits such as waiting period credit, provided they apply at least 45 days before the policy renewal date.
Day-care procedures that do not require 24-hour hospitalization, such as cataract surgery or dialysis, are covered under most modern health insurance policies.
The claim settlement ratio of a health insurer indicates the percentage of claims it has paid out of the total claims received in a financial year.
A mediclaim policy typically excludes claims arising from participation in adventure sports unless a specific rider is purchased.
The Third Party Administrator (TPA) is responsible for processing cashless claims, verifying hospital bills, and coordinating settlement between the hospital and the insurer.
Health insurance claims for maternity benefits usually become payable only after a waiting period of 9 months to 4 years, depending on the policy.
Under a family floater health insurance plan, the total sum insured is shared among all covered family members rather than assigned individually.
Insurers require an intimation of hospitalization within 24 to 48 hours for planned admissions and within 24 hours for emergency admissions to process a claim smoothly.
Ayush treatments such as Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy are covered under many health insurance policies up to the sum insured limit.
A no-claim bonus increases the sum insured or reduces the premium for policyholders who do not file any claim during a policy year.
Health insurance claim documents typically include the claim form, original bills, discharge summary, prescription, and diagnostic test reports.
Restoration benefit in a health insurance policy automatically reinstates the sum insured once it is exhausted by a claim in the same policy year.
To file a motor insurance claim after an accident, the policyholder must inform the insurer within 24 to 48 hours and file an FIR if the damage involves a third party or theft.
A motor insurance own-damage claim covers repair costs to the insured vehicle due to accident, fire, theft, or natural calamities, subject to policy terms.
No-claim bonus in motor insurance offers a discount on the premium for each claim-free year, and can range up to 50% after five consecutive years.
Third-party motor insurance is mandatory under law and covers liability for injury or damage caused to another person or their property.
A motor insurance claim can be settled on a cashless basis at a network garage or on a reimbursement basis after the policyholder pays for repairs upfront.
Zero depreciation cover in motor insurance ensures that the claim amount is not reduced for wear and tear of parts, unlike a standard own-damage claim.
Motor insurance claims are typically rejected if the vehicle was being driven without a valid license or under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident.
The Insured Declared Value (IDV) of a vehicle determines the maximum claim amount payable in case of total loss or theft under a motor insurance policy.
A life insurance death claim requires the nominee to submit the original policy document, death certificate, and a claim form to the insurer.
Life insurance policies typically become incontestable after 3 years, meaning the insurer cannot reject a death claim citing non-disclosure beyond that period except in cases of fraud.
A term life insurance policy pays the sum assured to the nominee only in the event of the policyholder's death during the policy term, with no maturity benefit.
Suicide within the first 12 months of a life insurance policy is generally excluded from claim payment, though most insurers refund the premiums paid.
Life insurance maturity claims are processed automatically at the end of the policy term if the policyholder survives, without requiring extensive documentation.
A life insurance policy lapses if the premium is not paid within the grace period, and a lapsed policy claim may be rejected unless the policy is revived.
Accidental death benefit riders on a life insurance policy pay an additional sum assured if death occurs due to an accident rather than natural causes.
Travel insurance claims for trip cancellation require proof of the reason for cancellation, such as a medical certificate or death certificate of a family member.
Emergency medical expenses incurred abroad are covered under travel insurance, subject to submission of hospital bills and a claim form after returning.
Baggage loss claims under travel insurance require a property irregularity report from the airline in addition to the claim form and boarding pass.
Travel insurance policies generally exclude claims arising from pre-existing medical conditions unless a specific waiver is purchased at the time of buying the policy.
A travel insurance claim for flight delay is payable only if the delay exceeds a specified number of hours, as mentioned in the policy schedule.
Travel insurance does not cover claims for trips undertaken against government advisories warning against travel to that destination.
Home insurance claims for fire or natural calamity damage require photographs of the damage, a list of affected items, and repair estimates.
Burglary claims under home insurance require a copy of the police complaint (FIR) along with a list of stolen items and their estimated value.
Home insurance policies typically exclude claims for damage caused by normal wear and tear or poor maintenance of the property.
Structure and contents can be insured separately or together under a home insurance policy, affecting how a claim is assessed and settled.
In India, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) mandates that health insurance claims be settled within 30 days of receiving all required documents.
IRDAI guidelines require insurers to clearly disclose all policy exclusions and waiting periods in the policy document before the free-look period expires.
An ombudsman can be approached by a policyholder to resolve a claim dispute if the insurer's internal grievance redressal process fails to provide a satisfactory resolution.
Insurance premiums and claim experience are reviewed annually by insurers, and features such as coverage limits or waiting periods may be revised at each policy renewal.
